model: frontier-model-A (an Anthropic frontier model: the session's serving model after the user switched the session's model during collection, per the Claude Code Remote session record of 2026-10-13; exact model identifiers are kept out of repository artifacts by this session's publication rule and are recorded in the session itself); every reply in this transcript is attributed to that model from its own agent transcript; no local open-source model was reachable from this container
invocation: Claude Code Workflow subagents, one fresh context per (item, arm, role), launched 2026-10-13 from session_01CLMsAqMfeDxCT9iN1dnaMh; each agent received the frozen system prompt verbatim (for the committee arm, prefixed 'Act as <role>. ' exactly as cortex/evaluation/arms.py does), read the item's user prompt from a file holding the exact canonical JSON the frozen arm would send, and returned {disposition, answer, confidence} through a structured-output call; replies were serialised to JSON and keyed by sha256(system + NUL + user)
tool_use: prohibited by instruction except one Read of the item's own prompt file; enforcement is post hoc: every agent transcript was audited (baseline-transcript-audit.json) and a reply with any other tool call is excluded from the transcript; the gold answers were never on any path the agents were pointed at
prompt_fidelity: system prompt byte-identical to arms.BASELINE_SYSTEM (sha256:e5ffbe9451a88600a36e2133ce48f2660f8483b9332fcad5e76017b73694b4d2); user prompt byte-identical to arms._prompt(item) over run.load_items (expanded payloads); delivered by file read rather than as an inline chat turn
limitations: the model is from the same vendor family as the agents that authored the held-out suite, so suite-authoring bias is not excluded; the agents' context held the harness instruction text in addition to the two prompts; cost is not metered per call and the frozen harness records 0.0 USD for the replayed arms, which can only favour the baselines on the cost criterion; latency is wall-clock of a Workflow agent, not of a model call, so the latency criterion is not comparable and is reported as such; collection was interrupted twice by session usage limits and resumed from cache; because the session's serving model changed between collections, 55 baseline replies and 5 semantic replies first served by frontier-model-B (the session's configured model before the switch) were re-collected under frontier-model-A with identical prompts, and the frontier-model-B replies are preserved as partial transcripts that no reported arm uses

semantic_transcript.model: frontier-model-A (the same model as the baseline arms; the semantic organ records this label on each sourced receipt)
semantic_transcript.invocation: Claude Code Workflow subagents, one fresh context per sourced item (5 prompts: SMOKE-SEM, H-S01, H-S02, H-S04, H-M02), launched 2026-10-13 from session_01CLMsAqMfeDxCT9iN1dnaMh (re-collected under frontier-model-A; the earlier frontier-model-B replies are preserved as a partial transcript); each agent read the organ's system prompt and the item's user prompt from two files holding the exact texts the organ sends (cortex.organs.semantic.SYSTEM_PROMPT and canonical_json({question, sources})) and returned {answer, claims, assumptions, contradictions, uncertainty} through a structured-output call; keyed by sha256(system + NUL + user)
semantic_transcript.tool_use: prohibited by instruction except two Reads (the two prompt files); audited post hoc from every agent transcript (semantic-transcript-audit.json): 5 of 5 replies show exactly those two Reads plus the structured output
semantic_transcript.limitations: same vendor family as the suite's authors; the exact-quote check inside the organ is what grounds the reply, not the model's assertion

model_attribution: per reply, from the 'model' field of the agent transcript's assistant messages; build_single_model.py keeps only replies from exactly one recorded model and excludes any reply whose agent shows more than one
